mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 over the previous month indicates strong labor market conditions, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS declines by more than 5% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong supply-side expansion, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it indicates a tight monetary policy in a low-unemployment environment, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight monetary policy with low unemployment
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% year-over-year signals a strong demand in the housing market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where HOUST increases by more than 10% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.5 percentage points over the previous month and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 150,000, it signals a strengthening labor market, which historically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < previous month - 0.5pp and PAYEMS > previous month + 150,000
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp and PAYEMS increases by more than 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a contraction in economic activity, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 decreases by more than 1% QoQ.
